fields.description:
With a key-set prev, keys present in both prev and curr route to `_compute_mutations_emit_both`
with an empty `local_fields`, producing ~516 mutations per pass that are provably inert but not free.
Skip them. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
Each inert mutation still drives one per-mutation loop iteration in the batch apply path
(`applier.py:639-640`), which calls `_recheck_drift` ->
`concurrency.snapshot_head(repo_root)` — **a `git rev-parse` subprocess** — before dispatching via `_apply_one`. So ~516 extra
git invocations per pass, ~516 `RECON: batch_outcome` stderr lines, ~516 outcome records in the
manifest, and an inflated `mutation_count` so a converged pass reports 516 instead of 0. It also
enlarges the HEAD-drift window. Under `BOOTSTRAP_STRICT` (cap 10) or `BOOTSTRAP_THROTTLE` (cap 100)
these compete for cap slots with genuine work (`apply_planning.py:90-101`) and can starve it —
production defaults to `LIVE` (cap `None`), so that risk is latent, not live.

## Approach
Define inert as an empty Jira-reachable outbound payload after branch-3 conflict resolution. Keep
the existing comparison/resolution logic in `_compute_mutations_emit_both`, compute the survival
test inline in `differ.py` (no `batch_dispatch` import), and retain only fields accepted by the
existing Jira update path (`summary`, `description`, `assignee`, `priority`, `status`) whose resolved
value differs from `jira_fields.get(field)`. Skip branch-3 `_emit` when no such fields remain. Do not
short-circuit merely because `local_fields` is falsy: Jira-side values in those Jira-reachable fields
can still produce a real clear/update payload.

Concrete examples: if Jira and local both contain `summary` and the resolved value differs from
Jira, the mutation is still emitted. If local is empty but Jira has `summary`, the resolved `None` is
emitted because it is Jira-reachable and differs from Jira. If only a local bookkeeping/metadata field
changes, the mutation is inert because that field would be stripped before `update_issue`; branch-3
drops it before creating a mutation.


## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] With a key-set prev over a real corpus, `(outbound, update)` mutations with an empty effective
      payload are **0** (down from ~516). Tier: **unit** on `compute_mutations` + the corpus script.
- [ ] Mutations with a genuine non-empty effective payload are still emitted unchanged — the
      negative control. Tier: **unit**.
- [ ] `mutation_count` on a converged pass is 0. Tier: **integration** asserting the pass record.
- [ ] `git rev-parse` invocation count per pass equals the number of actually emitted mutations (0 on
      the converged-pass case in AC3). Tier: **integration** with a counting shim.

## Files
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/differ.py`, tests

Scope: S. Depends on A4-2.
